thought.text: The 403 is likely because I didn't save the `code_verifier` cookie set on the very first `/app/` hit (I used `-o /dev/null` without `-c`). Let me redo the entire flow with a single cookie jar from the start.

reasoning_content:
The oauth2 callback returned 403 Forbidden. Let me look at the details — this is likely a CSRF/state mismatch or the code was already used. Let me check the body more carefully. The 403 in oauth2-proxy often means "invalid code" or "redirect URI does not match" or the session_state was consumed. 

Actually, the issue: the callback needs a `code_verifier` cookie that was set during the initial PKCE flow. When I first did the auth URL, the oauth2-proxy set a code_verifier cookie. But I saved cookies to cj.txt starting with the auth GET... wait, actually the auth redirect went to Keycloak, so the code_verifier cookie was set by localhost:3000's oauth2-proxy when I hit /app/ the first time. Let me check — in step 1 I used `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' http://localhost:3000/app/` WITHOUT -c cj.txt, so I did NOT save the code_verifier cookie! Then in step 2 I started fresh with `-c cj.txt` for the Keycloak auth page, which has different cookies.

So the code_verifier cookie (set by oauth2-proxy on the first /app/ hit) is missing from my cookie jar. That's why the callback fails with 403. This is a flaw in MY test, not the installation.

Let me redo the whole flow cleanly with a single cookie jar from the very first /app/ hit.

action.command:
cd /tmp && rm -f c.txt kc2.html after2.html app2.html
# Step 1: first /app/ hit WITH cookie jar (captures code_verifier + session from oauth2-proxy)
AUTH=$(curl -s -b c.txt -c c.txt -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' http://localhost:3000/app/)
echo "captured cookies:"; grep -vE '^\#' c.txt | awk '{print $6}'
echo "auth: ${AUTH:0:90}..."
# Step 2: Keycloak auth page
curl -s -b c.txt -c c.txt -o kc2.html "$AUTH"
ACTION=$(sed -n '/<form/,/<\/form>/p' kc2.html | grep -oE 'action="[^"]+"' | head -1 | sed 's/action="//;s/"//' | sed 's/&/\&/g')
# Step 3: login
curl -s -b c.txt -c c.txt -o after2.html -w 'login: %{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n' \
  --data-urlencode "credentialId=" \
  --data-urlencode "username=spark@example.com" \
  --data-urlencode "password=SparkLocalPassw0rd!" \
  --data-urlencode "login=Sign In" "$ACTION"
